relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: He left Weimar to become a student at the University of Göttingen in 1809.

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: He studied metaphysics, psychology and logic under Gottlob Ernst Schulze, the author of Aenesidemus, who made a strong impression and advised him to concentrate on Plato and Immanuel Kant.

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: He arrived at the newly founded University of Berlin for the winter semester of 1811–12.

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: Arthur attended lectures by the prominent post-Kantian philosopher Johann Gottlieb Fichte

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: He also attended the lectures of the famous Protestant theologian Friedrich Schleiermacher, whom he also quickly came to dislike.

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: He attended philological courses by August Böckh and Friedrich August Wolf

relations.subject: Arthur Schopenhauer
relations.evidence: Another important experience during his stay in Weimar was his acquaintance with Friedrich Majer—a historian of religion, orientalist and disciple of Johann Gottfried Herder—who introduced him to Eastern philosophy
